item.title: NVIDIA XBAR Overclocking on Linux: an mVolt+ Alternative
item.description:
Intro

In my homelab, I run an Ubuntu gaming/AI VM with PCIe pass-through of an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060. After stumbling on r/overclocking and seeing people get great results overclocking Blackwell cards, I wanted to see how far I could push mine.

Windows users have been getting huge gains on RTX 50-series using mVolt+, which overclocks the Crossbar (XBAR) interconnect and tweaks the MSVDD voltage rail. On Linux, however, neither nvidia-smi nor LACT support it.

item.title: Enabling SR-IOV for an Intel X540-T2 on Proxmox 8
item.description:
Intro

In the quest to get more performance out of my inter-vm communication, I stumbled upon SR-IOV and virtual functions. I then purchased a 10gbe X540-T2 from a Chinese seller on eBay making sure to get one with a fan, as reports of this specific card say it runs quite hot. After setting everything up, I increased my network performance from 2.5gbps on a vSwitch to 14gbps with virtual function passthrough.

item.title: iDRAC 9 manual fan control on Dell PowerEdge servers
item.description:
Intro

I recently acquired a Dell Poweredge T440, and after installing a GPU the fans skyrocketed. This turned the server into a noise machine. To solve this, I created a script that disables third-party PCI mode and based on a threshold, set the fan speed to 20% or to be controlled by Dell’s fan profile. These are the steps I took to make my T440 silent again.

Downgrading iDRAC 9 firmware to 3.30.30.30

For this whole setup to work, iDRAC needs to be on firmware 3.30.30.30, as later firmware revisions remove the ability to control the fan speed. The firmware can be downloaded from Dell’s website↗ (opens in a new tab). To downgrade, navigate to your iDRAC’s web admin page, and under Maintenance->System Update you can apply the downgrade. After the downgrade, make sure IPMI over LAN is enabled under iDRAC Settings->Connectivity->Network->IPMI Settings.

item.title: Disk passthrough for vms in Proxmox
item.description:
Intro

It has always been recommended to give ZFS full disk control, so after placing my raid card in HBA mode, I mapped each whole disk to my TrueNAS vm.

INFO

item.title: Homelab
item.description:
Intro

This post describes my homelab setup so I can link it where needed (like in my resume). It changes all the time as I add things and break others, so this is how it looks as of November 2026. Most of the pieces below have their own post with the actual steps.

Hardware

Everything runs on a single Dell PowerEdge T440 with Proxmox VE 9.

Dell PowerEdge T440

  • 2x Xeon Gold 6126 (24 cores, 48 threads)
  • 256GB ECC RAM
  • Intel X540-T2 dual port 10GbE
  • PNY GeForce RTX 5060 8GB
  • 2x 1.92TB Samsung PM863a SSD (mirrored, VM disks)
  • 2x 1.92TB SSD, 2x 14TB IronWolf and 2x 8TB Toshiba HDD (passed through to TrueNAS)

After adding a GPU the fans turned the server into a noise machine, so I run them with manual iDRAC fan control. Two YuanLey switches with 2.5GbE ports and 10G SFP+ uplinks connect it to the rest of the house, and a TerraMaster F2-220 running DSM holds the backups.
